previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A man with end-stage renal disease, type I diabetes, and severe coronary artery disease underwent a quadruple coronary artery bypass graft (CABG x4) for revascularization. Postoperatively, he remained intubated overnight and was extubated on postoperative day one. He experienced transient hyperglycemia requiring ICU readmission and insulin regimen adjustment with endocrinology consultation. A serosanguinous sternal wound drainage prompted a course of cephalexin, and a moderate left pleural effusion was noted but remained asymptomatic. He received hemodialysis throughout the admission and a single unit of packed red cells for anemia. He was successfully weaned from inotropic support, transferred to the floor, and cleared for discharge home on postoperative day seven with home health services. Discharge instructions emphasized wound care, activity restrictions, and close monitoring for signs of infection or fluid overload.

INDICATION:  Right leg infection, query DVT.

ULTRASOUND-GUIDED ASPIRATION OF A FLUID COLLECTION, ___

INDICATION:  ___ man with vein harvest site infection.  For aspiration
of fluid and for Gram-stain and culture.

PROCEDURE:  The risks, benefits, and alternatives to the procedure were
described to the patient via a ___ interpreter.  Written informed consent
was obtained.  A pre- procedure timeout was performed using three patient
identifiers.

Preliminary ultrasound examination of the right lower extremity in the region
of cellulitic change demonstrates diffuse skin thickening with a complex
collection measuring roughly 3.5 x 1.2 x 3.9 cm. There is no internal
vascularity.

A suitable site for aspiration was chosen, and the overlying skin was prepped
and draped in usual sterile fashion.  Lidocaine 1% was infiltrated into the
skin and subcutaneous tissues as local anesthetic.  Under ultrasound guidance,
an 18-gauge spinal needle was advanced into the collection.  Approximately 14
cc of sanguinopurulent material was aspirated.  Sample was sent for Gram-stain
and anaerobic and aerobic culture.  Post-aspiration images demonstrated near-
total collapse of the cavity.

The patient tolerated the procedure well, without immediate complication.

Dr. ___ attending physician, was present for and participated in the
procedure in its entirety.

IMPRESSION:  Successful aspiration of fluid collection within the subcutaneous
tissues of the right lower extremity, yielding 14 cc of sanguinopurulent
material.

HISTORY:  ___ male status post CABG, evaluate for ileus.

COMPARISON:  ___.

ABDOMEN, FOUR VIEWS:  Median sternotomy wires and surgical clips are
visualized within the lung bases.  The left lower lobe is consolidated with
air bronchograms, and a small left pleural effusion.

There are no dilated loops of small or large bowel, without evidence of
obstruction or ileus.  No free air or pneumatosis is identified. High-density
intraluminal contents within the bladder likely reflect contrast related to
recent CTA performed ___.

IMPRESSION:
1.  No evidence of obstruction or ileus.
2.  Left lower lobe consolidation with air bronchograms, with a small left
pleural effusion.

TYPE OF EXAMINATION:  Chest PA and lateral.

INDICATION:  Evaluate pleural effusion, status post bypass surgery.

FINDINGS:  PA and lateral chest views were obtained with patient in upright
position.  Analysis is performed in direct comparison with the next previous
AP portable chest examination of ___.  Status post sternotomy with
moderate cardiac enlargement and moderate degree of mediastinal shift towards
the right.  The previously described densities occupying the left lung base
and obliterating the diaphragmatic contour persists.  The density extends
along the left lateral wall up to the hilar area and fills the corresponding
posterior pleural sinus.  Mild degree of right-sided pleural effusion also
exists and is seen to extend in the posterior region as well.  In comparison
with the next previous study of ___, no new parenchymal abnormalities have
developed and the described pleural densities appear stable.  The chest CT
examination of ___ is also reviewed and shows a sizeable left lower
lobe atelectasis coexisting with the pleural effusion.

ULTRASOUND-GUIDED ASPIRATION, ___

INDICATION:  ___ man status post CABG.  Cellulitis and fluid
collection near site of vein graft harvest.

PROCEDURE:  The risks, benefits, and alternatives to the procedure were
described to the patient, who gave written informed consent.  A preprocedure
timeout was performed using three patient identifiers. Preliminary scan over
the right lower extremity was performed, with attention to the inner thigh
through the right proximal calf.  Since the previous examination, the extent
of fluid appears much greater, extending from approximately the proximal thigh
through the proximal calf. The width of the fluid collection measured
approximately 2 cm. The entire area was prepped and draped in the usual
sterile fashion. Given the extent of the collection, two separate puncture
sites were planned. Lidocaine was infiltrated into the skin and subcutaneous
tissues for local anesthetic. Aspiration was performed of the proximal and
distal aspects of the collection via three passes through two separate
punctures. Approximately 35 cc of thick, sanguinopurulent fluid were
aspirated.

The patient tolerated the procedure without immediate complication.

Dr. ___ attending physician, was present for and participated in the
procedure in its entirety.

IMPRESSION:  Successful ultrasound-guided aspiration of a right lower
extremity fluid collection.  Approximately 35 cc of thick fluid were obtained.
The extent of the collection has increased since the previous aspiration
procedure of ___.
